title: 5 Successful Counterfeiters
summary: Josh and Chuck profile five successful counterfeiters: Stephen Burrows (18th-century con man who posed as a preacher, escaped from jail by setting it on fire, later became a benefactor in Canada and wrote Memoirs of My Own Life); the Lavender Hill Mob (1990s British counterfeiting and knockoff perfume ring led by Stephen Jury and printer Kenneth Mainstone, who also made fake stamps and fooled the Bank of England into redesigning the twenty pound note); the Nazi Operation Bernhard counterfeiting of British pound notes using concentration camp prisoner printers, laundered to undermine the British and US economies (later depicted in The Counterfeiters); Charles Ulrich (1860s New York engraver and polygamist who was betrayed by his women, escaped across the Niagara River, and was sentenced in Cincinnati); and Frank Abagnale Jr. (teen check forger and impostor, subject of Catch Me If You Can). The episode closes with listener mail about synesthesia (seeing words, colors, and numbers as colors) and a story about a sympathetic wrist injury. Note: the transcript is a machine transcription and some names and details are garbled; the Nazi operation is named Operation Bernhard and the film is The Counterfeiters.
topics: Nazi counterfeiting of British pound notes

segments.title: Opening banter and introduction to counterfeiting
segments.summary: Hosts banter about the film Dianne and counterfeiting as a dying art, admiring the daring of successful counterfeiters, and say the episode will cover five of them chronologically. Includes a sponsor read for GoToMeeting near the start.

segments.title: Stephen Burrows
segments.summary: Stephen Burrows, an 18th-century mischievous boy and impostor who posed as a ship doctor and a church leader, was jailed for passing counterfeit money, escaped by setting the jail on fire, fled to Canada, led a counterfeiting ring, then reformed, tutored wealthy children, founded a library, and wrote Memoirs of My Own Life.

segments.title: The Lavender Hill Mob
segments.summary: A 1990s British counterfeiting ring led by Stephen Jury and printer Kenneth Mainstone. They made fake pound notes and stamps, fooled UV detectors, led the Bank of England to change the twenty pound note design, and Jury was credited with starting the knockoff perfume market. Jury wrote Loads of Money.
topics: Bank of England twenty pound note

segments.title: Nazi Operation Bernhard counterfeiting of British pound notes
segments.summary: The Nazis ran a counterfeiting operation called Operation Bernhard, using concentration camp prisoners who were printers to forge about 650 million British pound notes. The aim was to undermine the British and US economies through inflation. The money was laundered through a German businessman, and the operation ended with the Allies destroying the equipment as the camp was liberated. Adolf Burger wrote a book that became The Counterfeiters.

segments.title: Charles Ulrich
segments.summary: Charles Ulrich, a 1860s New York engraver of plates and polygamist, was recruited by a mob, formed his own gang, was betrayed by his women, was tried in Cincinnati and sentenced to twelve years, and escaped across the Niagara River into Canada.

segments.title: Frank Abagnale and Catch Me If You Can
segments.summary: Frank Abagnale forged checks and posed as a pilot, doctor, and lawyer between ages 16 and 21, cashing over 2.5 million dollars in fake checks. The hosts compare the film Catch Me If You Can with real events, including his escape from a plane, his posing as a federal agent, his family situation, and his later work in security consulting.

segments.title: Sponsor read and outro
segments.summary: Brief GoToMeeting sponsor read, website pointer for image search, and closing.

segments.title: Listener mail on synesthesia and a sympathetic wrist injury
segments.summary: Listeners describe synesthesia: seeing words, numbers and letters as colors, and music as colors and explosions. Another listener describes a childhood wrist pain that matched a friend's injury. The hosts ask for listener email and social media contact.
